attrs.evidence: None, and GPT-5.6's reason for wanting it is the sharpest thing in the ruling: THE CURRENT PROGRAM IS CIRCULAR. The graph is compiled into an AF, the AF defines the labels, and ASR-COMPILE-AF then asks whether the compilation preserves the labels — preserves them relative to WHAT independent source evaluator? There is none. Until a native semantics exists, `semantics-preserving` has no referent and the question cannot be answered rather than merely being unanswered. This is the same species as R6's finding that the semantics CHOICE was not observable while the compilation choice was, one level further down.
attrs.gap: Nothing has been attempted. The three propositions ASR-NATIVE-SEMANTICS, ASR-COMPILE-DUNG and ASR-COMPILE-PRESERVES are a research programme, not a backlog item, and this round only records the split.
attrs.prior_art: GPT-5.6, ruling on INV-R7.3. It also warns against assuming Dung must be the native substrate: SRC-ADF-2014 introduced Abstract Dialectical Frameworks precisely as a generalisation with per-node acceptance conditions, which may fit typed support/attack more naturally, with Dung remaining a useful derived projection.

readjudicated.method: question_survives — an OPEN claim asserts nothing that could transfer; the question is re-posed against the target tree
readjudicated.note: The source-lane status is recorded in imported_from.source_status as provenance. This field records that the TARGET lane re-established it; the two are separate facts and the gate reads this one.

attrs.review_focus: The honest risk is that this is a large piece of work adopted because an auditor named it, at a moment when the artifact has no consumer for it. Nothing downstream currently needs a native semantics; §9 computes labels and no decision reads them.
attrs.statement: The semantics of the typed Mosaic assurance graph can be defined directly, without reference to an abstract argumentation framework.
